title: Zoning-rule review register: let it hold CALCULATION entries beside rule entries, and add the calculation entries for the first building option's path (floor area, lot coverage by portion, building-option floor stack, legal dwelling-unit limit, preliminary apartment estimate) with the complete comparison — expected from the independent reference cases, actual recomputed through the program by the test; legal requirements told apart from design assumptions; the coverage gaps stated; no rule, no calculation, no result, no fixture and no human verdict changed [D-090 R686-R707, R379]
objective: Extend the zoning-rule review register so it can carry CALCULATION entries (combined-rule and arithmetic calculations that have no rule file of their own) beside the 23 rule entries, by the register's existing process — authored source register.json, rendered by render_review_register.py, checked by check_review_register.py, tested by the register test suite — and add the calculation entries for the first building option's path for the benchmark lot (BBL 4073340070). Add a sibling 'calculations' list to register.json (the 23 'entries' stay byte-identical); bump schema_version 1.0 -> 1.1 additively. Each calculation entry carries: the law[] of every rule it combines (so the source of each is traceable), the register rule-entry ids it combines, its implementing code module(s) with per-module LF-normalized sha256 (its recorded identity, since there is no rule file), dedicated inputs/units/measurement_basis/formula/rounding fields (point 3), interpretation and implemented-vs-planned, a legal_vs_design marking of every figure (LEGAL REQUIREMENT with quoted text, or CHOSEN DESIGN ASSUMPTION; 700 sq ft and 0.60-0.75 labelled 'preliminary assumption'), a worked example whose EXPECTED side is the independent reference case (step-P5, real-lot, step-P6) and whose ACTUAL side is recomputed through the scenario engine by the test (agree / differ / side-missing), linked_records to the measurement-basis / reference cases / coverage matrix, test_links and an automated_tests result bound to the code-module digests, revision/last_changed, the standard human_review block (no verdict entered; applies-to-current derived from the code-module digests + law digests + revision), gaps and a coverage_gap sentence, and the standing draft_note. Add the calculation entries covering the six steps: calc-floor-area-allowance (FAR x recorded lot area = 20,150), calc-lot-coverage-by-portion (corner 100% + interior strip 80%), calc-building-option-floor-stack (footprint, each floor's area and height, total floor area, building height), calc-legal-dwelling-unit-limit (floor area / 680, round up at .75), and calc-preliminary-apartment-estimate (floor area x share / size). State every coverage gap from the inventory, including that the scenario three-answers engine and the M5-T144 engine change move no rule entry. Regenerate the Markdown; change NO rule file, NO scenario/calculation code, NO result, NO fixture and NO human verdict. The expected side of the entries that need the step-P6 independent example (lot coverage by portion, building-option floor stack, apartment estimate) binds once M4-T037 is accepted; calc-floor-area-allowance and calc-legal-dwelling-unit-limit can be completed now from the already-committed reference cases. THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RULINGS C1 to C9, at the end of the path notes, govern wherever they differ from the text above.
business_reason: The owner's message of 2026-10-09 (D-090 source-068, rows R685-R709) asks that the first building option be compared, step by step, with an independently worked example, and that the review register be kept current for every rule AND calculation, with each relevant page showing the five points, legal requirements told apart from design assumptions, combined calculations and their records linked, every gap stated, and human verdicts left to a named human reviewer. Today the register covers only the 23 rule files; the scenario engine that turns those rules into the reported floor area, footprint, building option, unit limit and estimate has no entry, and nearly the whole building-option path is withheld with no register page comparing it to an independent example. This task is the program side of the comparison whose independent side M4-T037 (step P6) writes; it is the smallest change that makes the register hold calculations and traces the first building option's path. It is part of the existing work toward the building option (R707), not a separate project.

path_notes: DESIGN (plain words). (1) New collection, not new fields on the 23. Add a sibling 'calculations' list to register.json beside 'entries'; the 23 rule entries keep their exact fixed key set and their rules/*.md pages byte-identical. schema_version moves 1.0 -> 1.1 (additive: a new collection and a new entry kind; old entries unchanged). The top-level key set in check_review_register.structure_errors gains 'calculations'; the field_guide gains a calculation sub-guide and an entry_kind value. (2) A calculation entry's fields: entry_id; entry_kind='calculation'; title; family; law[] (same shape as a rule entry, one per combined rule/section, so point 1 is carried and every source is traceable); combines_rule_ids[] (the register rule-entry ids it combines); code_modules[] = [{path, sha256}] and a single derived code_identity_sha256 = sha256 over the sorted 'path:sha256' lines (THIS is how an entry with no rule file is identified and fingerprinted; the checker recomputes each module's LF-normalized sha256 and the combined identity, and fails if a module changed and the entry was not revised, exactly as rule_file_errors does for a rule entry); applicable_from/applicable_to (the latest last_amended among the combined rules); applies_where; exceptions[]; interpretation; inputs[]; units; measurement_basis; formula; rounding (point 3 as DEDICATED fields; where no rounding rule exists the field reads 'none - no rounding rule'); behaviour{tested,committed_untested,planned} (implemented vs planned, point 2); legal_vs_design[] (one row per figure/step: kind LEGAL_REQUIREMENT with quoted_text + capture digest, or DESIGN_ASSUMPTION; the 700 sq ft size and 0.60-0.75 share rows carry the literal words 'preliminary assumption'); example{description, inputs, expected{values, basis_kind(reference_case|law_text|gap), basis(the named case#row or measurement-basis example), prepared_by}, actual{values, state}, agrees(true|false|null)}; linked_records[] (measurement-basis, reference cases, coverage matrix - linked not copied, R702); test_links[]; automated_tests{...} bound to code_identity_sha256 and the test-file digests (same staleness rule: a changed module or test file forces status 'Not run'); revision; last_changed; human_review (the SAME block as a rule entry, but applies_to_current is derived from reviewed_code_identity_sha256 + reviewed_law_digests + reviewed_revision versus current - so a decision never survives a code change; no verdict is entered); gaps[]; coverage_gap (one plain sentence for R703); draft_note. (3) Rendering. calc detail pages render to docs/zoning-rule-review/calculations/<id>.md (a NEW folder, so they do not trip the rules/*.md orphan sweep in rendered_errors); REGISTER.md gains a 'Calculations' table section; HISTORY.md already carries any entry_id. The calc renderer and the calc checker helpers live in ONE new focused module review_register_calculations.py, imported by both render_review_register.py and check_review_register.py (old import paths kept as thin facades) to keep both files inside the modularity thresholds. (4) Files and growth: register.json grows by the calculation entries and history events (JSON data, not SLOC-limited); check_review_register.py (498 SLOC) and render_review_register.py (423) grow only by the wiring (top-level key, calculations loop, delegation ~20-40 lines each, staying under the 600 warn line - run python3 tools/modularity_check.py --check, warn 600 / justify 750 / hard 1000); the bulk goes in review_register_calculations.py (new, focused, well under 600); the new test file test_zoning_rule_review_register_calculations.py goes in the existing owned folder services/api/tests/rules/ (do NOT grow the 538-line test_zoning_rule_review_register.py). (5) The existing 23 entries stay valid WITHOUT being rewritten: no new field is added to them; the point-3 fields (units/measurement_basis/formula/rounding) exist only on calculation entries, and their absence on the 23 rule entries is stated as a coverage gap (inventory item 6) rather than back-filled in this task - so 'optional for the existing entries' resolves to 'not added here, listed as a gap'. (6) What a reviewer must check by hand: that the history was appended and never rewritten (the check reads only the current file); that each expected value truly comes from the named independent record and NOT from a program run; that legal_vs_design is correct and 700/0.60-0.75 read 'preliminary assumption'; that no human_review decision was entered. (7) ONE entry or several? SEVERAL - one calculation entry per combining-calculation seam, because the entry's example holds a single expected/actual pair while the six steps have different inputs/units/measurement/formula/rounding, different code identities and different current states (floor area available-conditional; footprint, floor stack and estimate withheld or not built; unit limit withheld though the engine computes it). The set: calc-floor-area-allowance, calc-lot-coverage-by-portion, calc-building-option-floor-stack (covers 'each floor's area and height' and 'total floor area' together, as they come from one stack), calc-legal-dwelling-unit-limit, calc-preliminary-apartment-estimate; property inputs (step 1) are documented as the shared inputs/measurement_basis of calc-floor-area-allowance plus the recorded-vs-measured lot-area note, not a sixth entry, to keep the task smallest. (8) Complete today vs waiting for step-P6: calc-floor-area-allowance (expected from step-p5-worked#floor-area-ratio and real-lot#L1, both committed; actual 20,150 available) and calc-legal-dwelling-unit-limit (expected 29 from real-lot#L6, committed; actual withheld) can be COMPLETE now. calc-lot-coverage-by-portion, calc-building-option-floor-stack and calc-preliminary-apartment-estimate WAIT for the step-P6 case; the fields that wait are example.expected.values, example.expected.basis (the step-p6-worked#row id), example.agrees, and the per-building structured numbers; until M4-T037 is accepted those keep basis_kind 'gap' and agrees null. RULINGS (the orchestrator's, after reading the draft against the code): C1 (one page for the whole calculation). Beside the five component entries add ONE calculation entry for the first building option's complete calculation on the benchmark lot: six steps in order (property inputs; footprint; each floor's area and height; total floor area; applicable legal unit limit; the separate preliminary apartment estimate), each step with the independent example's answer (named case#row), the program's actual answer and its standing (settled, conditional, withheld, not built), and one of: agree / differ (by how much, and why) / a side is missing; each step links its component entry or rule entry. It ends in the list of every disagreement and missing fact, each with its kind (a missing fact about the property; unresolved law; code not built; a design assumption that differs) and what would settle it. C2 (where the program's side comes from). The document-level actual answer is read from the committed results document packages/contracts/fixtures/valid/results/recorded_215_16_northern_journey.json, which the journey test proves equal, byte for byte, to what the program emits; a figure the engine computes and the document withholds (the unit count; the sample floor stack) is recomputed by the register's own test through the engine's functions from inputs stated in the entry, and the page says both: what the engine computes and that the document withholds it. The test imports nothing from another test folder. The expected side is never taken from a program run. C3 (the case exists). Task M4-T037 is integrated at the claim base, so docs/reference-cases/R6B/cases/step-p6-worked.json exists: no entry waits for it. An expected answer cites its case#row; a cited row that does not exist, or is superseded, is refused by the checker. Where the two readings of the case differ on a figure, the entry's expected side holds both figures, named, and agrees is null with the reason. C4 (a difference of method is a disagreement). The engine's sample building stacks floors on a plate of lot area times coverage up to the height limit; the independent example works a widest same-plan building up to the floor-area allowance and a second one to the minimum base height. Record it as a disagreement of kind 'a design assumption that differs', with backlog row DB-210 (the recorded lot area against the outline's area; which building the first option shows: the owner's decision, pending). Do not resolve it and do not change the engine. C5 (the 23 rule entries stay as they are). They are not rewritten in this task. That their pages lack dedicated fields for units, measurement basis, formula and rounding is stated in the coverage-gap list, with the six entries on this path named; each calculation page carries those five fields for its own steps, the rule's formula and rounding included, so the path is traceable now. C6 (the coverage-gap list is data). The list lives in register.json as its own top-level list, is rendered into REGISTER.md, and holds at least the nine gaps of the inventory (drafts/register-coverage-inventory.md, section E), each a plain sentence; the guide's own list of code with no rule id is brought into line with it. C7 (no revision of a rule entry moves; history is appended). Each new entry starts at revision 1 with a 'created' history event; no existing history line changes. No human verdict is entered; the human-review block of a calculation entry is the same as a rule entry's, with the recorded identity being the code identity, the law digests and the revision. C8 (the existing test file). services/api/tests/rules/test_zoning_rule_review_register.py is not in the allowed paths. If the new collection cannot be added without changing it, STOP and report which assertion and why. C9 (gates). G0, G2, G3 (data-contract-verifier: each entry against its sources, the cases and the program's real output), G4 (qa-engineer: the tests and mutations); no G5: no dependency, no route, no ledger tool changes.
